lines.text: A hundred six feet of ship. A hundred ten feet of lock. Two feet to spare.
This is Panama. Almost fourteen thousand ships a year. One every thirty eight minutes.
The original locks, built in 1914, are three and a half football fields long. Ships are built to fit that box.
Think parallel parking, but the car is nine hundred sixty five feet long.
But no ship steers itself in two feet. So electric locomotives called mules hold it with cables from both walls.
No pumps. Gravity pulls in twenty six million gallons from the lake. About forty Olympic pools.
Three steps. Eighty five feet up.
In 2016, new locks opened. Ships twelve hundred feet long fit, with about six feet to spare, guided by tugboats.
That ship is longer than the Eiffel Tower is tall.
One ship every thirty eight minutes. Two feet at a time.
Next time: what happens when the lake runs dry.
